docs.title: solarff
docs.text:
Extrapolation of the solar coronal magnetic field from SDO/HMI vector magnetograms, with a calibrated confidence for every field line.

A nonlinear force-free (NLFFF) extrapolation gives a full 3D field, but not all of it deserves the same trust. solarff computes the extrapolation and then tells you, line by line, how likely each field line is to reproduce the true geometry.

docs.title: What it does
docs.text: Task Functions Potential, linear and nonlinear force-free extrapolation potential_field, lfff, nlfff_lbfgs, nlfff Preprocessing of the vector magnetogram preprocess Field-line tracing trace_field_lines, seeds_from_magnetogram Per-line confidence assess_lines, confidence_map, reliable_volume Free energy and relative helicity with their uncertainties helicity_report, monte_carlo Twist, decay index and squashing factor Q twist_map, decay_index_profile, squashing_q Download and reading of SHARP data, sunpy interoperability download_sharp, load_sharp_cea, from_sunpy, to_sunpy PDF report of a region run_study, generate_report

docs.title: The idea in one figure
docs.text:
The confidence is a logistic regression on three indicators of each line: the variation of the force-free parameter α along it, the fraction of the line inside the boundary layer of the extrapolation, and its length. It is calibrated on exact force-free fields, where the true error of every line is known, and validated by leaving out one whole family of fields at a time.

With the default threshold (confidence ≥ 0.8) about half of the lines are accepted, and about 4 % of the accepted ones are wrong, against about 30 % of all lines.

docs.title: Per-line confidence
docs.text: Every traced line gets a confidence between 0 and 1, defined as one minus the estimated probability that the line is wrong. A line is wrong when its mean distance to the true line traced from the same seed exceeds 10 % of the length, or when one of the two is open and the other closed.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
import solarff as sff

mag = sff.load_sharp_cea("data/harp377", rebin=4).balance_flux()
nl = sff.nlfff_lbfgs(sff.preprocess(mag), nz=48)

seeds = sff.seeds_from_magnetogram(mag, n=300)
lines = sff.trace_field_lines(nl, seeds)

a = sff.assess_lines(nl, lines, mag=mag)
a["confidence"]      # one value per line
a["reliable"]        # boolean mask: confidence >= 0.8
a["indicators"]      # the indicators the confidence is computed from

Two more helpers build on it:

cm = sff.confidence_map(nl, mag=mag, step=2)            # confidence of the line leaving each pixel
vol = sff.reliable_volume(nl, lines, a["reliable"])     # 3D mask of cells threaded by reliable lines

docs.title: How it was calibrated
docs.text:
• Training set: six families of exact force-free fields (three Low & Lou variants, two exact linear fields and a relaxed Titov–Démoulin flux rope), three noise models, three grid sizes and boxes of four proportions (the standard one, two flat ones and a tall one). That is 162 extrapolations and 48 062 lines whose true error is known.
  • Model: a logistic regression with five terms: the variation of α along the line, the fraction of the line in the boundary layer, and the logarithm of the length relative to the horizontal diagonal of the box, its square, and the logarithm of the length relative to the height of the box. No more complex classifier does better.
  • Why the height of the box: a model fitted in boxes of one proportion accepts 8 to 11 % of wrong lines in boxes as flat as those of real regions. With the last term the figure is 4 to 6 % in every box, also in boxes left out of the fit. In four external families the term halves the wrong lines accepted in flat boxes, but it does not even them out: an external flux rope stays at 10 % there, against 3 % in the standard box, and in a tall box the term accepts 2 to 5 points more than the four terms. The model of version 1.1, without that term, is kept as solarff.confidence.CALIBRATION_V1.
  • Validation: leaving out one whole family at a time, so the model is always tested on a geometry it has not seen.
Threshold Lines accepted Wrong among the accepted 0.7 62 % 8.4 % 0.8 (default) 51 % 4.4 % 0.9 37 % 1.5 %

On an independent flux rope that was never used for training, the wrong lines among the accepted ones drop from 34 % to 3 %.

docs.title: Applying it to your own extrapolation
docs.text:
1. Use the same code and the same preprocessing. The preprocessing is the critical choice: with other parameters the confidence degrades and does not notice.
  2. Check the range of the extrapolation. The mean current-weighted angle CWsin should be within 0.04–0.21, the divergence energy fraction E_div/E within 0.006–0.24 and the boundary weight within 0.03–0.48. Outside these ranges, do not use the published probability.
  3. Pick the threshold for your use. Use 0.9 if almost no accepted line may be wrong, 0.7 to keep more lines.
  4. Report results on reliable lines too. If a per-line quantity changes when restricted to reliable lines, say by how much.
  5. Do not attribute energy to a zone of the volume without repeating the calculation with different seed densities, dilations and thresholds.
  6. With another NLFFF code, recalibrate with the same procedure (examples/04_calibration_suite.py).

Read it as a conditional score

Passing the range checks is necessary, not sufficient. For real magnetograms the confidence is a conditional reliability score, not a guaranteed error probability. Within one region, use it above all to rank lines.

docs.title: Known limits
docs.text:
• Optimistic cases that nothing flags. On four external families the ranking holds (AUC 0.86–0.95), but in two of them 18–21 % of the accepted lines are wrong. Their wrong lines look like good ones to the indicators, and no global quantity of the extrapolation warns of it. A high failure rate is not the criterion: another external family fails on a similar fraction of lines and its accepted set stays clean.
  • Systematic errors in the magnetogram. A scale error of ±30 % in the transverse field, or taking it one cell higher than the vertical field, barely changes the result. A systematic rotation of the azimuth does: at about 5° or more the probability becomes optimistic, and at 10° the ranking degrades as well. The force and torque balance of the magnetogram (Aly criteria) does not reveal it.
  • Idealised training fields. The calibration fields have an exactly force-free photosphere. Real photospheres do not. On exact fields built on the observed flux of three regions, and on the models of those regions taken as the truth, the ranking holds (AUC 0.76–0.93) but the accepted lines are wrong about twice as often as in the calibration suite (median 9 %, up to 25 %).
  • Resolution. The extrapolations of real regions are not converged. With half the pixel, more than half of the accepted lines move by more than 10 % of their length and the free energy changes by up to 26 %. The confidence ranks the lines by how little they depend on the resolution and on the unobserved boundaries, but an accepted line is not thereby a converged one.
  • One code. The published coefficients are valid for the solver in this library.

The coefficients are in solarff.confidence.DEFAULT_CALIBRATION. The full analysis is in the associated paper.

docs.title: Energy and helicity
docs.text:
rep = sff.helicity_report(nl)

helicity_report computes, for a 3D field:

  • the potential field with the same normal flux on the six faces of the box;
  • the energy decomposition of Valori et al. (2013), where E_div/E measures how much energy is spurious because of the residual divergence;
  • the relative helicity in the DeVore gauge with two references, whose difference is the numerical error of the helicity.

The free energy can be defined as the difference with the potential field (E − E_p) or as the energy of the current-carrying part (E_J). They differ by 4–19 % in the regions studied, so always state which one you quote.

docs.title: Is the region eruptive?
docs.text:
Function What it computes Usual threshold twist_map(field), twist_number(field, lines) twist number Tw of each line (Berger & Prior 2006; Liu et al. 2016) abs(Tw) ≳ 1: flux rope decay_index_profile(pot) decay index n(z) of the potential field above the inversion line, and the critical height (Kliem & Török 2006) n ≥ 1.5: torus unstable squashing_q(field) squashing factor Q at the base (Titov et al. 2002; Pariat & Démoulin 2012) Q ≫ 2: quasi-separatrix layer

For the decay index, compute the potential field with pad=2. The periodic copies of the Fourier solution distort the decay with height otherwise.

docs.title: Uncertainties: Monte Carlo with the HMI errors
docs.text:
mag = sff.load_sharp_cea("data/harp377", rebin=4).balance_flux()    # also reads the *_err segments
study = sff.run_study(mag, nz=48)
mc = sff.monte_carlo(study, n=10)
sff.generate_report(study, "docs/informes/my_region", monte_carlo=mc)

The preprocessing and the NLFFF are repeated with noise drawn from the HMI error maps. The result is the median and the 16–84 % interval of the free energy, the helicity, the critical height and the twist.

These are lower bounds

The Monte Carlo errors include neither systematic errors, nor ambiguity-resolution errors, nor the dependence on the extrapolation method.

docs.title: Noise bias
docs.text: Noise shifts some quantities systematically, so the Monte Carlo median does not match the nominal value. A bootstrap correction was tested on exact fields (examples/05_bias_validation.py). It helps with isotropic noise but makes things worse with HMI-like noise, where the transverse noise is much larger than the vertical one. It is therefore not applied, and the bias is reported as a systematic uncertainty. The free energy relative to the volume potential and the helicity are much more robust to noise.

docs.title: Known limitations
docs.text:
• LFFF. Periodic lateral boundaries, and abs(α) must stay below 2π/L. A single α does not represent regions with localised currents.
  • NLFFF. The side and top faces are fixed to the potential field, so results are reliable only away from them. Grids above about 128³ are slow.
  • Geometry. Cartesian, with no curvature, valid for regions up to about 200–300 Mm.
  • Uncertainties. The Monte Carlo errors are lower bounds: they exclude systematic errors and the dependence on the method.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
solarff needs Python 3.10 or later.

git clone https://github.com/gabgarar/solarff.git
cd solarff
python -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate          # Windows: .venv\Scripts\activate
pip install -e ".[all]"

docs.title: First run: an exact solution
docs.text:
Before using real data, check the installation against the analytical field of Low & Lou (1990). This takes about a minute.

import solarff as sff

mag, exact = sff.low_lou_magnetogram(nx=32, ny=32, nz=24, noise=10.0)

pot = sff.potential_field(mag, nz=24)
nl = sff.nlfff_lbfgs(sff.preprocess(mag), nz=24)

seeds = sff.seeds_from_magnetogram(mag, n=200)
models = {"Exact": exact, "Potential": pot, "NLFFF": nl}
sff.print_table(sff.compare_models(models, reference="Exact", seeds=seeds))
sff.plot_comparison(models, seeds, save="lowlou_lines.png")

docs.title: Real data: an HMI active region
docs.text:
The input is the SHARP product in cylindrical equal-area projection, hmi.sharp_cea_720s, which is already a vector magnetogram on a local Cartesian grid with the 180° ambiguity resolved.

Segment Meaning In the library Br radial component Bz Bp φ component (westward) Bx = Bp Bt θ component (southward) By = -Bt

Downloading needs an email address registered at JSOC. It is only passed to JSOC and never stored.

import solarff as sff

sff.search_sharp("2011-02-15T00:00:00", noaa=11158)          # find the HARP number
folder = sff.download_sharp(377, "2011-02-15T00:00:00", email="you@example.org")

mag = sff.load_sharp_cea(folder, rebin=4).balance_flux()
study = sff.run_study(mag, nz=48)      # potential + LFFF + preprocessing + NLFFF

Practical advice:

  • Use regions within 30–45° of the central meridian. Farther out the transverse noise grows quickly.
  • Reduce the resolution with rebin=2..4. A full-resolution SHARP is not tractable.
  • The geometry is Cartesian, valid for regions up to about 200–300 Mm.

docs.text:
import sunpy.map
import solarff as sff

mag = sff.from_sunpy(sunpy.map.Map("Br.fits"), sunpy.map.Map("Bp.fits"), sunpy.map.Map("Bt.fits"), rebin=4)
maps = sff.to_sunpy(mag)               # {"Br": Map, "Bp": Map, "Bt": Map}

docs.title: A PDF report of a region
docs.text:
study = sff.run_study(mag, nz=48)
sff.generate_report(study, "docs/informes/my_region")     # report in English and Spanish

The report needs LaTeX (MiKTeX or TeX Live). Without it, the .tex files are left ready to compile elsewhere.

Console messages

Progress messages printed by the solvers and the command-line help of the example scripts are still in Spanish. The API, the docstrings and this documentation are in English.

docs.title: Method and equations
docs.text: This page puts the library in context: the physical problem, the equations each step solves, and what goes in and comes out of every function.

docs.title: The problem
docs.text:
The magnetic field of the solar corona stores the energy released in flares and eruptions, but it cannot be measured directly. What is measured routinely is the vector field at the photosphere. The coronal field is then extrapolated from that boundary, assuming that in the low corona the magnetic force dominates and the field is close to force-free:

\[ ( abla imes\mathbf{B}) imes\mathbf{B} = 0, \qquad abla\cdot\mathbf{B} = 0 . \]

The first equation says the electric current is parallel to the field, so it can be written with a scalar, the force-free parameter \(\alpha\):

\[ abla imes\mathbf{B} = \alpha\,\mathbf{B}, \qquad \alpha = rac{( abla imes\mathbf{B})\cdot\mathbf{B}}{B^2}, \qquad \mathbf{B}\cdot abla\alpha = 0 . \]

The last relation follows from taking the divergence: in an exact solution \(\alpha\) is constant along each field line. Three models of increasing realism follow from what is assumed about \(\alpha\).

Model Assumption Boundary data needed Potential \(\alpha = 0\) (no currents) \(B_z\) Linear force-free (LFFF) \(\alpha\) constant everywhere \(B_z\) and one value of \(\alpha\) Nonlinear force-free (NLFFF) \(\alpha\) varies from line to line \(B_x\), \(B_y\), \(B_z\)

The NLFFF is the realistic one, but it is an ill-posed numerical problem: the photosphere is not force-free, the side and top boundaries are unknown, and the data are noisy. The result is a field that is good in some places and wrong in others. The per-line confidence is the tool to tell them apart.

docs.title: The pipeline
docs.text:
flowchart LR

    B --> C["NLFFF<br/>extrapolation"]

    E --> F["Confidence<br/>0 to 1"]
    C --> G["Energy, helicity,<br/>twist, Q"]

Each step is one function call:

docs.text:
Magnetogram, the photospheric boundary on a local Cartesian grid.

Attribute Meaning Units bx, by, bz field components, arrays of shape (nx, ny); bz is vertical G bx_err, by_err, bz_err 1σ uncertainty per pixel, if known G dx pixel size Mm origin coordinates of pixel [0, 0] Mm meta header information —

docs.title: Step 1: preprocessing
docs.text:
The photospheric field is not force-free, so it is not a consistent boundary for a force-free solution. A consistent boundary must have zero net force and zero net torque (Aly 1989). The library measures the departure with

\[ \epsilon_F = \frac{\left|\sum B_xB_z\right| + \left|\sum B_yB_z\right| + \left|\sum (B_z^2 - B_x^2 - B_y^2)\right|}{\sum (B_x^2+B_y^2+B_z^2)} , \]

and an analogous \(\epsilon_T\) for the torque (aly_criteria). Following Wiegelmann, Inhester & Sakurai (2006), the magnetogram is modified slightly by minimising

\[ L_{\rm pre} = \mu_1 L_1 + \mu_2 L_2 + \mu_3 L_3 + \mu_4 L_4 , \]

where \(L_1\) is the net force, \(L_2\) the net torque, \(L_3 = \sum|\mathbf{B}-\mathbf{B}_{\rm obs}|^2\) the distance to the data and \(L_4 = \sum|\Delta\mathbf{B}|^2\) the smoothness. Each term is normalised by its mean, so the weights do not depend on the size or strength of the magnetogram.

Parameter Default Meaning mu1, mu2 1 weight of the force and torque terms mu3 10⁻² how far the result may move from the data mu4 10⁻² how much it is smoothed fix_bz False modify only the transverse components

Warning

The confidence is calibrated with these defaults. Changing mu3 or mu4 degrades it without notice.

docs.title: Step 2: extrapolation
docs.text:
Potential and linear fields are solved in Fourier space (Alissandrakis 1981). Each horizontal mode \(\mathbf{k}\) of \(B_z\) at the base decays with height as \(e^{-\sqrt{k^2-\alpha^2}\,z}\), which requires \(|\alpha| < 2\pi/L\) for a box of side \(L\). potential_field(mag, nz) is the case \(\alpha = 0\), and lfff(mag, alpha, nz) the general one.

The NLFFF minimises a functional over the volume (Wheatland et al. 2000; Wiegelmann 2004):

\[ egin{aligned} L ={}& \left\langle w\left[ rac{|( abla imes\mathbf{B}) imes\mathbf{B}|^2}{B^2+\varepsilon^2} + w_d\,| abla\cdot\mathbf{B}|^2 ight] ight angle_V \ &+ u\left\langle W\,|\mathbf{B}_t-\mathbf{B}_{t, m obs}|^2 ight angle_{z=0} + \lambda\left\langle| abla^2\mathbf{B}|^2 ight angle_V . \end{aligned} \]

The first term is the force and the divergence, the second lets the transverse field at the base adjust within the noise (Wiegelmann & Inhester 2010), and the third penalises grid-scale oscillations. The weighting function \(w\) is 1 in the interior and falls to 0 in a buffer layer of nd cells next to the side and top boundaries, which are fixed to the potential field. The gradient is exact, by automatic differentiation, and the minimiser is L-BFGS.

Parameter of nlfff_lbfgs Default Symbol and meaning nz required number of grid levels in height nd max(4, min(nx, ny, nz)/10) width of the buffer layer, in cells relax_bottom 0.1 \( u\), freedom of the transverse field at the base eps 0.03 \(\varepsilon\) in units of max abs(\(B_z\)), regularisation near nulls smooth 10⁻² \(\lambda\), smoothness div_weight 1 \(w_d\), weight of the divergence term max_iter, tol 2000, 10⁻⁶ stopping criteria

The output is a VectorField3D. Its quality is summarised by the current-weighted angle between \(\mathbf{J}\) and \(\mathbf{B}\),

\[ \mathrm{CW}_{\sin} = rac{\sum_i |\mathbf{J}_i|\,\sigma_i}{\sum_i |\mathbf{J}_i|}, \qquad \sigma_i = rac{|\mathbf{J}_i imes\mathbf{B}_i|}{|\mathbf{J}_i|\,|\mathbf{B}_i|}, \]

which is 0 for an exactly force-free field, and by the fractional flux \(\langle|f_i| angle\), which measures the residual divergence.

docs.title: Step 3: field lines
docs.text:
A field line is the solution of \(d\mathbf{r}/ds = \mathbf{B}/|\mathbf{B}|\). It is integrated in both directions from a seed with fourth-order Runge–Kutta on the trilinearly interpolated field.

Parameter of trace_field_lines Default Meaning seeds required array (N, 3) of starting points, in Mm ds 0.5 integration step, in cells max_steps 4000 maximum steps per direction

seeds_from_magnetogram(mag, n, threshold, polarity) places n seeds where abs(\(B_z\)) exceeds threshold times its maximum. Each FieldLine holds its points in Mm, its seed and whether both ends are at the base (closed).

docs.title: Step 4: indicators and confidence
docs.text:
Three quantities are computed on each extrapolated line, with no knowledge of the true field.

Indicator Definition Why it reveals a wrong line Variation of α \(x_1 = \log_{10}\) of the spread of \(\alpha\) along the line, relative to its mean \(\alpha\) must be constant along a line of an exact solution Buffer fraction \(x_2\) = fraction of the line inside the buffer layer there the field is set by unobserved boundaries Length \(x_3 = \log_{10}(L/D)\), with \(D\) the horizontal diagonal of the box, and \(x_4 = (x_3 + 0.54)^2\) long lines accumulate error; very short ones fail in flux ropes

They are combined in a logistic regression. The probability that a line is wrong is

\[ p = \frac{1}{1+\exp\left[-\left(\beta_0+\sum_i \beta_i z_i\right)\right]}, \qquad z_i = \frac{x_i-\mu_i}{\sigma_i}, \]

and the confidence is \(1 - p\). The published coefficients, with \(\beta_0 = -1.33\), are:

Term \(x_i\) \(\mu_i\) \(\sigma_i\) \(\beta_i\) \(\log_{10}\) (variation of α) −0.788 0.606 +0.79 buffer fraction 0.166 0.277 +0.79 \(\log_{10}(L/D)\) −0.543 0.313 +1.12 \((\log_{10}(L/D)+0.54)^2\) 0.098 0.162 +0.78

The whole model fits in this table, so it can be applied without the library.

Output of assess_lines(field, lines, mag):

Key Content confidence array with one value in [0, 1] per line reliable boolean array, confidence ≥ threshold threshold the acceptance threshold, 0.8 by default indicators dictionary with every indicator of every line

docs.title: How the coefficients were obtained
docs.text:
A line is labelled wrong by comparing it with the exact line traced from the same seed. Both are parametrised by normalised arc length \(s\) and the shape error is

\[ \epsilon = \frac{1}{L_{\rm ref}}\int_0^1 \left|\mathbf{r}_{\rm NLFFF}(s)-\mathbf{r}_{\rm ref}(s)\right|ds . \]

A line is wrong if \(\epsilon > 0.1\) or if it changes between open and closed. The model is then judged by:

Measure Definition Question it answers AUC probability that a wrong line gets a higher \(p\) than a good one does it rank the lines? ECE \(\sum_m \frac{\lvert B_m\rvert}{n}\,\lvert\bar y(B_m)-\bar p(B_m)\rvert\) over 10 bins of \(p\) can the probability be read literally? Brier score \(\frac{1}{n}\sum_i (p_i-y_i)^2\) both at once Risk–coverage fraction of wrong lines among those kept, against the fraction kept which threshold suits my use?

docs.title: Step 5: energy, helicity and topology
docs.text:
With \(\mathbf{B}_p\) the potential field that has the same normal component on the six faces of the box, the energy is decomposed following Valori et al. (2013). Two free energies are given:

\[ E_{\rm free} = E - E_p, \qquad E_J = \frac{1}{8\pi}\int_V |\mathbf{B}-\mathbf{B}_p|^2\,dV , \]

which coincide only if the field is solenoidal. The fraction \(E_{\rm div}/E\) measures how much of the energy is spurious because of the residual divergence.

The relative magnetic helicity (Finn & Antonsen 1985) is

\[ H_V = \int_V (\mathbf{A}+\mathbf{A}_p)\cdot(\mathbf{B}-\mathbf{B}_p)\,dV , \]

with the vector potentials in the DeVore gauge. It is computed with two reference faces, and the difference between them is the numerical error of the helicity.

Output of helicity_report(field):

Key Content Units energy E, E_p, E_free, E_J, E_div, E_div_frac and the other terms of the decomposition erg helicity H_V, H_J, H_PJ and ratio_HJ_HV, gauge referred to the top face Mx² helicity_bottom_gauge the same, gauge referred to the bottom face Mx² gauge_diff relative difference between the two gauges — potential the reference potential field \(\mathbf{B}_p\) G

Three more diagnostics describe whether a region can erupt:

Quantity Definition Function Twist number \(T_w = \dfrac{1}{4\pi}\displaystyle\int \alpha\,dl\) along each line twist_map, twist_number Decay index \(n(z) = -\dfrac{d\ln B_h}{d\ln z}\) of the potential field above the inversion line decay_index_profile Squashing factor \(Q\), how strongly the line mapping between footpoints distorts a small circle squashing_q

A flux rope is usually taken as abs(\(T_w\)) ≳ 1, torus instability as \(n \geq 1.5\), and a quasi-separatrix layer as \(Q \gg 2\).

docs.title: Units and conventions
docs.text:
• Field in gauss, lengths in megametres, energy in erg, helicity in Mx².
  • Axes: \(x\) westward, \(y\) northward, \(z\) vertical. From SHARP: \(B_x = B_p\), \(B_y = -B_t\), \(B_z = B_r\).
  • The geometry is Cartesian, with no curvature, valid for regions up to about 200–300 Mm.

docs.title: Reproducing the paper
docs.text: Every figure, table and number of the associated paper is produced by a script in examples/.

docs.title: One command
docs.text:
sh tools/reproduce_all.sh you@example.org          # everything, in order
sh tools/reproduce_all.sh "" calib                 # only one phase

The email is only passed to JSOC for the downloads and can be empty if the data are already in data/. The phases are:

Phase What it runs Rough time on an 8-core laptop calib calibration suite in boxes of four proportions, noise bias, robustness, flux ropes and external families 5–7 h regiones the three active regions before and after each flare, with Monte Carlo 6–8 h analisis AIA comparison, flare energies, systematic base errors, tables and figures 1–2 h revision additional statistical and physical checks a few hours pruebas tests beyond the calibration suite: resolution and unobserved faces in the regions, fields built on the observed flux, region models taken as the truth about 8 h

docs.title: solarff.tracing
docs.text: Field-line tracing (vectorised RK4, trilinear interpolation).

docs.title: FieldLine dataclass
docs.text:
Field line in physical coordinates (Mm).

points is ordered in the direction of B: the first point is the "outgoing" end (positive polarity if the line is closed) and the last the "incoming" end (negative polarity).

Source code in solarff/tracing.py 
@dataclass
class FieldLine:
    """Field line in physical coordinates (Mm).

    ``points`` is ordered in the direction of B: the first point is the
    "outgoing" end (positive polarity if the line is closed) and the last the
    "incoming" end (negative polarity).
    """

    points: np.ndarray       # (M, 3)
    seed: np.ndarray         # (3,)
    closed: bool             # both ends at the base (z ≈ 0)

    @property
    def start(self):
        return self.points[0]

    @property
    def end(self):
        return self.points[-1]

    @property
    def length(self) -> float:
        return float(np.linalg.norm(np.diff(self.points, axis=0), axis=1).sum())

    @property
    def apex(self) -> float:
        return float(self.points[:, 2].max())

docs.title: integrate_lines
docs.text:
integrate_lines(field: VectorField3D, start_idx: ndarray, sign: float, scalar: ndarray | None = None, ds: float = 0.25, max_steps: int = 20000, b_min: float = 1e-06)

Integrate lines from start_idx (3, N) (grid indices) in one direction without storing the intermediate points.

Returns (endpoint (3, N) in indices, length (N,) in cells, integral of scalar along the line (N,) in cell units). Meant for thousands of lines (Q and Tw maps).

Source code in solarff/tracing.py 
def integrate_lines(field: VectorField3D, start_idx: np.ndarray, sign: float,
                    scalar: np.ndarray | None = None, ds: float = 0.25,
                    max_steps: int = 20000, b_min: float = 1e-6):
    """Integrate lines from ``start_idx`` (3, N) (grid indices) in one direction
    without storing the intermediate points.

    Returns (endpoint (3, N) in indices, length (N,) in cells, integral of
    ``scalar`` along the line (N,) in cell units). Meant for
    thousands of lines (Q and Tw maps).
    """
    fa = (field.bx, field.by, field.bz)
    upper = np.array(field.shape, dtype=float) - 1
    pos = np.clip(np.asarray(start_idx, dtype=float).copy(), 0, upper[:, None])
    n = pos.shape[1]
    length = np.zeros(n)
    integ = np.zeros(n)
    active = np.ones(n, dtype=bool)
    for _ in range(max_steps):
        if not active.any():
            break
        ia = np.flatnonzero(active)
        p = pos[:, ia]
        k1, b = _direction(fa, p, sign)
        k2, _ = _direction(fa, p + 0.5 * ds * k1, sign)
        k3, _ = _direction(fa, p + 0.5 * ds * k2, sign)
        k4, _ = _direction(fa, p + ds * k3, sign)
        newp = p + ds / 6 * (k1 + 2 * k2 + 2 * k3 + k4)
        newp, out = _stop_at_boundary(p, newp, upper)
        stop = out | (b < b_min)
        seg = np.linalg.norm(newp - p, axis=0)
        length[ia] += seg
        if scalar is not None:
            integ[ia] += map_coordinates(scalar, 0.5 * (p + newp), order=1, mode="nearest") * seg
        pos[:, ia] = newp
        active[ia[stop]] = False
    return pos, length, integ

docs.title: trace_field_lines
docs.text:
trace_field_lines(field: VectorField3D, seeds: ndarray, ds: float = 0.5, max_steps: int = 4000, b_min: float = 0.001) -> list[FieldLine]

Trace field lines from seeds (array (N, 3) in Mm) in both directions.

ds is the step in cell units. Using the same seeds in different models allows their connectivity to be compared.

Source code in solarff/tracing.py 
def trace_field_lines(field: VectorField3D, seeds: np.ndarray, ds: float = 0.5,
                      max_steps: int = 4000, b_min: float = 1e-3) -> list[FieldLine]:
    """Trace field lines from ``seeds`` (array (N, 3) in Mm) in both directions.

    ``ds`` is the step in cell units. Using the *same* seeds in
    different models allows their connectivity to be compared.
    """
    seeds = np.atleast_2d(np.asarray(seeds, dtype=float))
    origin = np.asarray(field.origin, dtype=float)
    idx0 = ((seeds - origin) / field.dx).T  # (3, N)
    upper = np.array(field.shape, dtype=float) - 1
    idx0 = np.clip(idx0, 0, upper[:, None])
    fa = (field.bx, field.by, field.bz)

    fwd = _trace_one_direction(fa, idx0, +1.0, ds, max_steps, upper, b_min)
    bwd = _trace_one_direction(fa, idx0, -1.0, ds, max_steps, upper, b_min)

    lines = []
    z_tol = 1.0  # cells
    for j in range(seeds.shape[0]):
        f = fwd[:, :, j]
        b = bwd[:, :, j]
        f = f[~np.isnan(f[:, 0])]
        b = b[~np.isnan(b[:, 0])]
        pts = np.concatenate([b[::-1], f[1:]], axis=0)
        pts_phys = pts * field.dx + origin
        closed = bool(pts[0, 2] <= z_tol and pts[-1, 2] <= z_tol and len(pts) > 3)
        lines.append(FieldLine(points=pts_phys, seed=seeds[j], closed=closed))
    return lines

docs.title: seeds_from_magnetogram
docs.text:
seeds_from_magnetogram(source: Magnetogram | VectorField3D, n: int = 80, threshold: float = 0.1, z: float | None = None, polarity: str = 'positive', method: str = 'grid', rng: int | None = 0) -> np.ndarray

Seeds to trace lines at pixels with |Bz| > threshold·max|Bz|.

Parameters

  • n: approximate number of seeds.
  • polarity: "positive" (default), "negative" or "both". Since each line is traced in both directions, seeding on a single polarity avoids drawing the same loop twice.
  • method: "grid" (regular grid over the selected region: also covers the weak field and gives cleaner figures) or "random" (probability proportional to |Bz|, concentrates in the cores).
  • z: height of the seeds (by default one cell above the base, to avoid the z = 0 layer, where the NLFFF is noisier).
Source code in solarff/tracing.py 
def seeds_from_magnetogram(source: Magnetogram | VectorField3D, n: int = 80,
                           threshold: float = 0.1, z: float | None = None,
                           polarity: str = "positive", method: str = "grid",
                           rng: int | None = 0) -> np.ndarray:
    """Seeds to trace lines at pixels with |Bz| > ``threshold``·max|Bz|.

    **Parameters**

    - ``n``: approximate number of seeds.
    - ``polarity``: ``"positive"`` (default), ``"negative"`` or ``"both"``. Since each
        line is traced in both directions, seeding on a single polarity avoids
        drawing the same loop twice.
    - ``method``: ``"grid"`` (regular grid over the selected region: also covers
        the weak field and gives cleaner figures) or ``"random"``
        (probability proportional to |Bz|, concentrates in the cores).
    - ``z``: height of the seeds (by default one cell above the base, to
        avoid the z = 0 layer, where the NLFFF is noisier).
    """
    if isinstance(source, VectorField3D):
        bz = source.bz[:, :, 0]
        dx = source.dx
        ox, oy, _ = source.origin
    else:
        bz, dx = source.bz, source.dx
        ox, oy = source.origin
    if z is None:
        z = dx
    signed = {"positive": bz, "negative": -bz, "both": np.abs(bz)}[polarity]
    mask = signed > threshold * np.abs(bz).max()
    gen = np.random.default_rng(rng)

    if method == "grid":
        ix, iy = np.nonzero(mask)
        # Grid step such that ~n seeds remain
        step = max(1.0, np.sqrt(mask.sum() / max(n, 1)))
        while True:
            gx = np.floor(ix / step)
            gy = np.floor(iy / step)
            key = gx * 1e6 + gy
            _, first = np.unique(key, return_index=True)
            if first.size <= n or step > max(bz.shape):
                break
            step *= 1.05
        # One point per grid cell: the one closest to the centre of the cell
        cx, cy = (gx + 0.5) * step, (gy + 0.5) * step
        d = (ix - cx) ** 2 + (iy - cy) ** 2
        order = np.lexsort((d, key))
        _, first = np.unique(key[order], return_index=True)
        sel = order[first]
        px, py = ix[sel].astype(float), iy[sel].astype(float)
    elif method == "random":
        cand = np.flatnonzero(mask.ravel())
        p = np.abs(bz).ravel()[cand]
        pick = gen.choice(cand, size=min(n, cand.size), replace=False, p=p / p.sum())
        px, py = np.unravel_index(pick, bz.shape)
        px = px + gen.uniform(-0.5, 0.5, px.size)
        py = py + gen.uniform(-0.5, 0.5, py.size)
    else:
        raise ValueError("method debe ser 'grid' o 'random'")
    return np.column_stack([ox + px * dx, oy + py * dx, np.full(px.size, z)])

docs.title: solarff.confidence
docs.text:
Reliability of each field line of a model.

For each traced line, indicators are computed that, without knowing the true solution, flag whether that part of the model can be trusted:

Indicator Meaning sin_jb mean sine of the J–B angle along the line, weighted by the current (0 = force-free) alpha_spread relative variation of α along the line (in a force-free field α is constant on each line) div mean relative divergence \(\langle \lvert\nabla\cdot\mathbf{B}\rvert\,\Delta x / 6\lvert\mathbf{B}\rvert \rangle\) over the line buffer fraction of the line inside the buffer layer, where the (unobserved) boundary rules open 1 if the line leaves through a side or the top of the domain foot_snr observed transverse field at the weakest footpoint divided by its noise (the α carried by the line is measured at the footpoint) base_change relative correction of the transverse field that the model applied at the footpoints (relaxed base): how much it ignored the data there apex maximum height of the line / height of the box (high lines depend more on the unobserved top) length length of the line / horizontal diagonal of the box length_h length of the line / height of the box (a line that is long compared with the height depends on the unobserved top, whatever the horizontal size of the box)

The indicators are combined into a confidence ∈ [0, 1] (1 − probability that the line is wrong) by a logistic regression calibrated with exact force-free fields with noise, where the true error of each line is known. The default calibration (DEFAULT_CALIBRATION) was fitted with the diverse suite of solarff.calibration (6 field families, 3 noise models, 3 resolutions and boxes of four proportions) and validated leaving out each family.

Limitation: these are necessary conditions, not sufficient ones. A line can be perfectly force-free and still be wrong if the data at its footpoint are consistently erroneous; that is only detected by noise ensembles, independent methods or coronal observations.

line_indicators(field: VectorField3D, lines: list[FieldLine], mag: Magnetogram | None = None, noise_bt: float = 100.0, nd: int | None = None) -> dict

Reliability indicators of each line (see the table of the module).

Parameters

  • field: 3D model (normally the NLFFF).
  • lines: lines traced in field.
  • mag: magnetogram used as boundary condition (the preprocessed one if there was one). Needed for foot_snr and base_change.
  • noise_bt: noise of the transverse field in G (~100 G in HMI).
  • nd: buffer layer (by default that of the model, meta["nd"]).
Source code in solarff/confidence.py 
def line_indicators(field: VectorField3D, lines: list[FieldLine], mag: Magnetogram | None = None,
                    noise_bt: float = 100.0, nd: int | None = None) -> dict:
    """Reliability indicators of each line (see the table of the module).

    **Parameters**

    - ``field``: 3D model (normally the NLFFF).
    - ``lines``: lines traced in ``field``.
    - ``mag``: magnetogram *used as boundary condition* (the preprocessed one if
        there was one). Needed for ``foot_snr`` and ``base_change``.
    - ``noise_bt``: noise of the transverse field in G (~100 G in HMI).
    - ``nd``: buffer layer (by default that of the model, ``meta["nd"]``).
    """
    h = field.dx
    origin = np.asarray(field.origin)
    jx, jy, jz = field.current()
    bx, by, bz = field.bx, field.by, field.bz
    fx, fy, fz = cross(jx, jy, jz, bx, by, bz)
    jxb = np.sqrt(fx ** 2 + fy ** 2 + fz ** 2)
    babs = field.babs
    jb = np.sqrt(jx ** 2 + jy ** 2 + jz ** 2) * babs
    alpha = np.nan_to_num(field.alpha(b_min_frac=0.0), nan=0.0, posinf=0.0, neginf=0.0)
    div = np.abs(field.divergence()) * h / (6 * np.maximum(babs, 1e-12 * babs.max()))
    nd = nd if nd is not None else field.meta.get("nd", max(4, min(field.shape) // 10))
    w = weight_function(field.shape, nd)
    upper = np.array(field.shape) - 1
    # reference α for normalisation (scale of the domain)
    alpha0 = 2 * np.pi / (max(field.shape[:2]) * h) * 0.1

    out = {k: np.full(len(lines), np.nan) for k in ALL_FEATURES + ("length_h",)}
    ztop = max(upper[2] * h, 1e-9)
    diag = np.hypot(*(upper[:2] * h))
    for i, l in enumerate(lines):
        p = l.points
        if len(p) < 3:
            continue
        idx = ((p - origin) / h).T
        seg = np.r_[np.linalg.norm(np.diff(p, axis=0), axis=1), 0.0]
        if seg.sum() <= 0:
            continue
        a_jxb = _interp(jxb, idx)
        a_jb = _interp(jb, idx)
        den = (a_jb * seg).sum()
        out["sin_jb"][i] = (a_jxb * seg).sum() / den if den > 0 else 0.0
        al = _interp(alpha, idx)
        wt = seg / seg.sum()
        m = (al * wt).sum()
        sd = np.sqrt(((al - m) ** 2 * wt).sum())
        out["alpha_spread"][i] = sd / (abs(m) + alpha0)
        out["div"][i] = (_interp(div, idx) * wt).sum()
        ww = _interp(w, idx)
        out["buffer"][i] = (wt * (ww < 0.99)).sum()
        ends = np.array([idx[:, 0], idx[:, -1]])
        on_side = ((ends[:, 0] <= 1e-6) | (ends[:, 0] >= upper[0] - 1e-6) |
                   (ends[:, 1] <= 1e-6) | (ends[:, 1] >= upper[1] - 1e-6) |
                   (ends[:, 2] >= upper[2] - 1e-6))
        out["open"][i] = float(on_side.any() or not l.closed)
        out["length"][i] = seg.sum() / diag
        out["length_h"][i] = seg.sum() / ztop
        out["apex"][i] = (p[:, 2].max() - origin[2]) / ztop

    if mag is not None and mag.has_vector:
        # Footpoints: endpoints at the base (z < 1 cell)
        bt_obs = np.hypot(mag.bx, mag.by)
        dbt = np.hypot(field.bx[:, :, 0] - mag.bx, field.by[:, :, 0] - mag.by)
        for i, l in enumerate(lines):
            if len(l.points) < 3:
                continue
            feet = [q for q in (l.points[0], l.points[-1]) if q[2] - origin[2] < h]
            if not feet:
                feet = [l.points[0]]
            fi = np.array(feet)
            gx = (fi[:, 0] - origin[0]) / h
            gy = (fi[:, 1] - origin[1]) / h
            bt = _interp2(bt_obs, gx, gy)
            out["foot_snr"][i] = float(bt.min() / noise_bt)
            out["base_change"][i] = float((_interp2(dbt, gx, gy) / np.maximum(bt, noise_bt)).max())
    else:
        out["foot_snr"][:] = 1.0
        out["base_change"][:] = 0.0
    return out

True error of each line with respect to the reference traced from the same seed.

shape: mean distance between the two lines sampled at the same fractions of length, relative to the length of the reference line. endpoint: mean distance between endpoints (Mm). topology: 1 if one is closed and the other open. shape_abs: the same mean distance in Mm (not divided by the length); length_ref / length_model: lengths (Mm). They allow "wrong line" to be redefined with an absolute threshold without tracing again.

Source code in solarff/confidence.py 
def line_errors(lines_model: list[FieldLine], lines_ref: list[FieldLine], n: int = 40) -> dict:
    """True error of each line with respect to the reference traced from the same seed.

    ``shape``: mean distance between the two lines sampled at the same
    fractions of length, relative to the length of the reference line.
    ``endpoint``: mean distance between endpoints (Mm).
    ``topology``: 1 if one is closed and the other open.
    ``shape_abs``: the same mean distance in Mm (not divided by the length);
    ``length_ref`` / ``length_model``: lengths (Mm). They allow "wrong line" to be
    redefined with an absolute threshold without tracing again.
    """
    shape = np.full(len(lines_ref), np.nan)
    shape_abs = np.full(len(lines_ref), np.nan)
    lref = np.full(len(lines_ref), np.nan)
    lmod = np.full(len(lines_ref), np.nan)
    endp = np.full(len(lines_ref), np.nan)
    topo = np.zeros(len(lines_ref))
    for i, (a, b) in enumerate(zip(lines_model, lines_ref)):
        if len(a.points) < 3 or len(b.points) < 3:
            continue
        def res(p):
            s = np.r_[0, np.cumsum(np.linalg.norm(np.diff(p, axis=0), axis=1))]
            t = np.linspace(0, s[-1], n)
            return np.stack([np.interp(t, s, p[:, k]) for k in range(3)], axis=1), s[-1]
        pa, la = res(a.points)
        pb, lb = res(b.points)
        shape_abs[i] = np.linalg.norm(pa - pb, axis=1).mean()
        shape[i] = shape_abs[i] / max(lb, 1e-9)
        lref[i], lmod[i] = lb, la
        endp[i] = 0.5 * (np.linalg.norm(a.start - b.start) + np.linalg.norm(a.end - b.end))
        topo[i] = float(a.closed != b.closed)
    return {"shape": shape, "endpoint": endp, "topology": topo, "shape_abs": shape_abs,
            "length_ref": lref, "length_model": lmod}

def length_in_heights(length, shape) -> np.ndarray:
    """Length of the lines in box heights (``length_h``) from ``length`` and the grid ``shape`` of the model.

    ``length`` is relative to the horizontal diagonal of the box. For per-line records saved before
    ``length_h`` existed: both indicators are the same length divided by two sizes of the same box.
    """
    nx, ny, nz = shape
    return np.asarray(length, dtype=float) * np.hypot(nx - 1, ny - 1) / max(nz - 1, 1)

Area under the ROC curve: probability that a wrong line has a higher score than a good one.

Source code in solarff/confidence.py 
def auc(score, bad):
    """Area under the ROC curve: probability that a wrong line has a higher ``score`` than a good one."""
    score, bad = np.asarray(score, float), np.asarray(bad, bool)
    ok = np.isfinite(score)
    s, b = score[ok], bad[ok]
    if b.all() or (~b).all():
        return float("nan")
    order = np.argsort(s)
    ranks = np.empty(len(s))
    ranks[order] = np.arange(1, len(s) + 1)
    # ties: mean rank
    _, inv, cnt = np.unique(s, return_inverse=True, return_counts=True)
    sums = np.bincount(inv, ranks)
    ranks = (sums / cnt)[inv]
    n1 = b.sum()
    return float((ranks[b].sum() - n1 * (n1 + 1) / 2) / (n1 * (len(s) - n1)))

Source code in solarff/confidence.py 
def confidence(ind: dict, calibration: dict | None = None) -> np.ndarray:
    """Confidence ∈ [0, 1] of each line (1 − estimated probability of being wrong)."""
    cal = calibration or DEFAULT_CALIBRATION
    if "length_h" in cal["features"] and "length_h" not in ind:
        raise KeyError("this calibration needs the indicator 'length_h' (length of the line in box heights); for indicators "
                       "saved without it, add ind['length_h'] = length_in_heights(ind['length'], shape of the model)")
    X = _design(ind, cal["features"])
    Z = (X - np.array(cal["mu"])) / np.array(cal["sd"])
    z = Z @ np.array(cal["coef"]) + cal["intercept"]
    p_bad = 1 / (1 + np.exp(-z))
    if cal.get("iso_x"):
        # isotonic recalibration (monotone table fitted out of sample)
        p_bad = np.interp(p_bad, cal["iso_x"], cal["iso_y"])
    c = 1 - p_bad
    c[~np.isfinite(c)] = np.nan
    return c

One calibration case: NLFFF model of mag, indicators and true error per line.

Variants: "coarse" (magnetogram rebinned by 2 and half the levels in height), "lfff" (side and top faces fixed to the LFFF of best-fit alpha instead of the potential field), "smooth" (three times the smoothing weight of the preprocessing). Unlike the Monte Carlo over the noise, they probe systematic errors.

exact: true field; mag: its base with noise (with *_err if mc is wanted). Returns {"ind", "err", "bad", "noise", "bad_threshold"} (and model, pp if keep_model). nlfff_kw and preprocess_kw are passed to the NLFFF and to the preprocessing (to study the robustness to their parameters).

def calibration_case(exact: VectorField3D, mag: Magnetogram, nz: int, n_seeds: int = 300,
                     bad_threshold: float = 0.1, method: str = "lbfgs", seed: int = 0,
                     noise_bt: float | None = None, mc: int = 0, gr: bool = False,
                     mc_seed: int = 1000, nlfff_kw: dict | None = None,
                     preprocess_kw: dict | None = None, keep_model: bool = False,
                     ensemble: tuple = ()) -> dict:
    """One calibration case: NLFFF model of ``mag``, indicators and true error per line.

    ``ensemble``: variants of the extrapolation in which something that is not known is changed; for each
    one, the displacement of every line with respect to the nominal model is stored as ``ens_<variant>``
    (mean distance relative to the length of the nominal line, as the shape error) and ``ens_<variant>_topo``
    (1 if the line changes between open and closed). Variants: ``"coarse"`` (magnetogram rebinned by 2 and
    half the levels in height), ``"lfff"`` (side and top faces fixed to the LFFF of best-fit alpha instead of
    the potential field), ``"smooth"`` (three times the smoothing weight of the preprocessing). Unlike the
    Monte Carlo over the noise, they probe systematic errors.

    ``exact``: true field; ``mag``: its base with noise (with ``*_err`` if
    ``mc`` is wanted). Returns ``{"ind", "err", "bad", "noise", "bad_threshold"}``
    (and ``model``, ``pp`` if ``keep_model``). ``nlfff_kw`` and ``preprocess_kw`` are
    passed to the NLFFF and to the preprocessing (to study the robustness to their parameters).
    """
    from .preprocess import preprocess
    from .tracing import seeds_from_magnetogram, trace_field_lines
    from .nlfff import nlfff

    def model_of(m):
        if method == "lbfgs":
            from .nlfff_torch import nlfff_lbfgs
            return nlfff_lbfgs(m, nz, verbose=False, **(nlfff_kw or {}))
        return nlfff(m, nz, verbose=False, **(nlfff_kw or {}))

    noise = float(mag.meta.get("noise", 0.0))
    noise_bt = noise_bt if noise_bt is not None else float(mag.meta.get("noise_t", noise)) or 100.0
    pp = preprocess(mag, verbose=False, **(preprocess_kw or {}))
    model = model_of(pp)
    seeds = seeds_from_magnetogram(mag, n=n_seeds, method="random", polarity="both",
                                   threshold=0.05, rng=seed)
    lm = trace_field_lines(model, seeds)
    le = trace_field_lines(exact, seeds)
    ind = line_indicators(model, lm, mag=pp, noise_bt=noise_bt)
    if mc:
        from .montecarlo import perturb
        rng = np.random.default_rng(mc_seed)
        good = np.zeros((mc, len(lm)), dtype=bool)
        for k in range(mc):
            if mag.has_errors:
                mk = perturb(mag, rng)
            else:
                mk = perturb(mag, rng, noise=noise)
            ek = line_errors(trace_field_lines(model_of(preprocess(mk, verbose=False, **(preprocess_kw or {}))),
                                               seeds), lm)
            good[k] = (ek["shape"] <= bad_threshold) & (ek["topology"] == 0)
        ind["mc_instability"] = 1 - good.mean(axis=0)
    if gr:
        from .grad_rubin import nlfff_grad_rubin
        dis = np.zeros((2, len(lm)))
        for j, pol in enumerate(("P", "N")):
            g = nlfff_grad_rubin(pp, nz, polarity=pol, verbose=False)
            eg = line_errors(trace_field_lines(g, seeds), lm)
            dis[j] = (eg["shape"] > bad_threshold) | (eg["topology"] > 0)
        ind["method_disagreement"] = dis.mean(axis=0)
    for v in ensemble:
        from .nlfff_torch import nlfff_lbfgs
        kw = nlfff_kw or {}
        if v == "coarse":
            pc = preprocess(mag.rebin(2), verbose=False, **(preprocess_kw or {}))
            mv = nlfff_lbfgs(pc, max(8, int(round(nz / 2))), verbose=False, **kw)
        elif v == "lfff":
            from .alpha import alpha_best_fit
            from .lfff import lfff
            mv = nlfff_lbfgs(pp, nz, initial=lfff(pp, alpha_best_fit(pp), nz), verbose=False, **kw)
        elif v == "smooth":
            kp = dict(preprocess_kw or {})
            kp["mu4"] = 3 * kp.get("mu4", 1e-2)
            mv = nlfff_lbfgs(preprocess(mag, verbose=False, **kp), nz, verbose=False, **kw)
        else:
            raise ValueError(f"variante desconocida: {v}")
        ev = line_errors(trace_field_lines(mv, seeds), lm)
        ind["ens_" + v] = ev["shape"]
        ind["ens_" + v + "_topo"] = ev["topology"]
    err = line_errors(lm, le)
    bad = (err["shape"] > bad_threshold) | (err["topology"] > 0)
    rec = {"ind": ind, "err": err, "bad": bad, "noise": noise, "bad_threshold": bad_threshold}
    if keep_model:
        rec.update(model=model, pp=pp)
    return rec

Generate the calibration data: Low & Lou + noise, NLFFF model and true error per line.

A line is considered wrong if its relative shape error exceeds bad_threshold (10 % of its length) or if it changes topology. With mc > 0 the indicator mc_instability is added: fraction of the mc realizations (observation + noise of the same level) in which the line no longer matches that of the nominal model. With gr=True method_disagreement is added: fraction of the Grad–Rubin solutions (P and N) in which the line does not match that of the model. checkpoint: file where each finished realization is saved; if it exists with the same configuration, it resumes from there.

@keeps_awake
def calibration_data(realizations: int = 3, n: int = 40, nz: int = 28, noise: float = 30.0,
                     n_seeds: int = 300, bad_threshold: float = 0.1, method: str = "lbfgs",
                     seed: int = 0, mc: int = 0, gr: bool = False, checkpoint: str | None = None,
                     verbose: bool = True) -> list:
    """Generate the calibration data: Low & Lou + noise, NLFFF model and true error per line.

    A line is considered *wrong* if its relative shape error exceeds
    ``bad_threshold`` (10 % of its length) or if it changes topology.
    With ``mc > 0`` the indicator ``mc_instability`` is added: fraction of the ``mc``
    realizations (observation + noise of the same level) in which the line
    no longer matches that of the nominal model.
    With ``gr=True`` ``method_disagreement`` is added: fraction of the Grad–Rubin
    solutions (P and N) in which the line does not match that of the model.
    ``checkpoint``: file where each finished realization is saved; if it exists
    with the same configuration, it resumes from there.
    """
    from . import analytic as an
    say = print if verbose else (lambda *a, **k: None)
    signature = {"realizations": realizations, "n": n, "nz": nz, "noise": noise, "n_seeds": n_seeds,
                 "bad_threshold": bad_threshold, "method": method, "seed": seed, "mc": mc, "gr": gr}
    state = load_checkpoint(checkpoint, signature)
    data = state["data"] if state is not None else []
    if data:
        say(f"  calibración: reanudando desde {checkpoint} ({len(data)}/{realizations} realizaciones hechas)")
    for r in range(len(data), realizations):
        mag, exact = an.low_lou_magnetogram(noise=noise, rng=seed + r, nx=n, ny=n, nz=nz)
        rec = calibration_case(exact, mag, nz, n_seeds=n_seeds, bad_threshold=bad_threshold,
                               method=method, seed=seed + 100 + r, noise_bt=noise, mc=mc, gr=gr,
                               mc_seed=seed + 1000 + r)
        data.append(rec)
        say(f"  realización {r}: {len(rec['bad'])} líneas, {rec['bad'].mean():.0%} malas")
        if checkpoint:
            save_checkpoint(checkpoint, {"signature": signature, "data": data})
    return data

def fit_calibration(data: list, features=("sin_jb", "alpha_spread", "buffer", "apex"),
                    max_bad_accepted: float = 0.2) -> dict:
    """Fit the confidence with all the realizations but the last and evaluate it on the last.

    Returns ``{"calibration": ..., "metrics": ...}``. The confidence threshold
    is the lowest one that leaves at most ``max_bad_accepted`` wrong lines among
    the accepted ones (in the test realization).
    """
    features = list(features)
    train, test = data[:-1], data[-1]
    Xtr = np.vstack([_design(d["ind"], features) for d in train])
    ytr = np.concatenate([d["bad"] for d in train]).astype(float)
    ok = np.all(np.isfinite(Xtr), axis=1)
    cal = _fit_logistic(Xtr[ok], ytr[ok])
    cal.update(features=features, bad_threshold=test["bad_threshold"], noise=test["noise"])
    ind, err, bad = test["ind"], test["err"], test["bad"]
    conf = confidence(ind, cal)
    per_feature = {k: auc(-np.asarray(ind[k], float) if k == "foot_snr" else np.asarray(ind[k], float), bad)
                   for k in ALL_FEATURES + tuple(x for x in ("mc_instability", "method_disagreement") if x in ind)}
    thr = 0.5
    for t in np.linspace(0.05, 0.95, 91):
        acc = conf >= t
        if acc.sum() >= 10 and bad[acc].mean() <= max_bad_accepted:
            thr = float(t)
            break
    acc = conf >= thr
    cal["threshold"] = thr
    metrics = {
        "auc_combined": auc(-conf, bad), "auc_features": per_feature, "threshold": thr,
        "bad_fraction_all": float(bad.mean()),
        "bad_fraction_accepted": float(bad[acc].mean()) if acc.any() else float("nan"),
        "accepted_fraction": float(acc.mean()),
        "error_median_accepted": float(np.nanmedian(err["shape"][acc])) if acc.any() else float("nan"),
        "error_median_rejected": float(np.nanmedian(err["shape"][~acc])) if (~acc).any() else float("nan"),
        "test_conf": conf, "test_err": err["shape"], "test_bad": bad,
    }
    return {"calibration": cal, "metrics": metrics}

def select_calibration(extras: tuple = ()) -> dict:
    """Calibration suited to the additional indicators available."""
    has_mc = "mc_instability" in extras
    has_gr = "method_disagreement" in extras
    if has_mc and has_gr and DEFAULT_CALIBRATION_MC_GR:
        return DEFAULT_CALIBRATION_MC_GR
    if has_gr and DEFAULT_CALIBRATION_GR:
        return DEFAULT_CALIBRATION_GR
    if has_mc and DEFAULT_CALIBRATION_MC and mc_gain_significant():
        return DEFAULT_CALIBRATION_MC
    return DEFAULT_CALIBRATION

def mc_gain_significant() -> bool:
    """Does the Monte Carlo stability improve the confidence significantly?

    The calibration with ``mc_instability`` is used only if the 95 % interval of
    its AUC gain (bootstrap paired by cases) excludes zero. With the
    first five families the gain was +0.009–0.011, but when the flux rope is
    added it vanishes (+0.001 [−0.003, +0.004]): on the rope the NLFFF
    is wrong in a way that is *stable* against noise (systematic error), so
    the stability does not tell the good lines from the wrong ones.
    """
    ci = CALIBRATION_METRICS_MC.get("auc_gain_mc_ci") if CALIBRATION_METRICS_MC else None
    return bool(ci) and ci[0] > 0

def assess_lines(field: VectorField3D, lines: list[FieldLine], mag: Magnetogram | None = None,
                 noise_bt: float = 100.0, calibration: dict | None = None,
                 extra: dict | None = None) -> dict:
    """Indicators, confidence and mask of reliable lines (confidence ≥ calibrated threshold).

    ``extra``: additional per-line indicators, e.g. ``{"mc_instability": ...}``
    from the Monte Carlo. If it includes ``mc_instability`` and no calibration is given,
    ``DEFAULT_CALIBRATION_MC`` is used.
    """
    if calibration is None:
        calibration = select_calibration(tuple(sorted(extra)) if extra else ())
    cal = calibration
    ind = line_indicators(field, lines, mag=mag, noise_bt=noise_bt)
    if extra:
        ind.update({k: np.asarray(v, float) for k, v in extra.items()})
    conf = confidence(ind, cal)
    return {"indicators": ind, "confidence": conf,
            "reliable": np.nan_to_num(conf, nan=0.0) >= cal["threshold"],
            "threshold": cal["threshold"],
            "calibration": "+".join(["base"] + [x for x in ("mc_instability", "method_disagreement") if x in cal["features"]])}

confidence_map(field: VectorField3D, mag: Magnetogram | None = None, step: int = 1, threshold: float = 0.05, noise_bt: float = 100.0, calibration: dict | None = None, extra: dict | None = None) -> dict

Confidence of the line leaving each pixel of the base (|Bz| > threshold·max).

Returns conf (2D), reliable (2D), x, y, the lines and their indicators (lines, assess) for reuse.

Source code in solarff/confidence.py 
def confidence_map(field: VectorField3D, mag: Magnetogram | None = None, step: int = 1,
                   threshold: float = 0.05, noise_bt: float = 100.0,
                   calibration: dict | None = None, extra: dict | None = None) -> dict:
    """Confidence of the line leaving each pixel of the base (|Bz| > ``threshold``·max).

    Returns ``conf`` (2D), ``reliable`` (2D), ``x``, ``y``, the lines and their
    indicators (``lines``, ``assess``) for reuse.
    """
    from .tracing import trace_field_lines
    bz = field.bz[:, :, 0]
    ix = np.arange(0, field.shape[0], step)
    iy = np.arange(0, field.shape[1], step)
    IX, IY = np.meshgrid(ix, iy, indexing="ij")
    strong = np.abs(bz[IX, IY]) > threshold * np.abs(bz).max()
    x0, y0 = field.origin[0], field.origin[1]
    seeds = np.column_stack([x0 + IX[strong] * field.dx, y0 + IY[strong] * field.dx,
                             np.full(strong.sum(), field.origin[2] + 0.5 * field.dx)])
    lines = trace_field_lines(field, seeds)
    a = assess_lines(field, lines, mag=mag, noise_bt=noise_bt, calibration=calibration, extra=extra)
    conf = np.full(IX.shape, np.nan)
    conf[strong] = a["confidence"]
    rel = np.zeros(IX.shape, dtype=bool)
    rel[strong] = a["reliable"]
    return {"conf": conf, "reliable": rel, "x": x0 + ix * field.dx, "y": y0 + iy * field.dx,
            "lines": lines, "assess": a, "strong": strong, "step": step}

reliable_volume(field: VectorField3D, lines: list[FieldLine], reliable: ndarray, dilate: int = 1) -> np.ndarray

3D mask of the cells threaded by reliable lines (dilated by dilate cells).

Source code in solarff/confidence.py 
def reliable_volume(field: VectorField3D, lines: list[FieldLine], reliable: np.ndarray,
                    dilate: int = 1) -> np.ndarray:
    """3D mask of the cells threaded by reliable lines (dilated by ``dilate`` cells)."""
    from scipy.ndimage import binary_dilation
    m = np.zeros(field.shape, dtype=bool)
    origin = np.asarray(field.origin)
    up = np.array(field.shape) - 1
    for l, ok in zip(lines, reliable):
        if not ok or len(l.points) < 2:
            continue
        idx = np.clip(np.rint((l.points - origin) / field.dx).astype(int), 0, up)
        m[idx[:, 0], idx[:, 1], idx[:, 2]] = True
    if dilate:
        m = binary_dilation(m, iterations=dilate)
    return m

docs.title: solarff.calibration
docs.text:
Rigorous calibration of the per-line confidence with diverse data.

Generates a suite of cases with known truth (several families of exact force-free fields, several noise levels and types and several resolutions; see solarff.analytic.CALIBRATION_FIELDS and NOISE_MODELS), and evaluates classifiers with cross-validation leaving out a whole field type (the classifier has never seen the geometry it is evaluated on), with bootstrap confidence intervals.

Metrics (see Niculescu-Mizil & Caruana 2005; Guo et al. 2017):

  • AUC: ranking ability (do the wrong lines get less confidence?).
  • Brier: mean squared error of the predicted probability.
  • ECE (expected calibration error): mean difference between the predicted probability and the observed frequency of wrong lines.

The comparison of classifiers uses scikit-learn (optional dependency, pip install scikit-learn); the rest does not need it.

def add_box(data: list) -> list:
    """Copy of the cases with ``nz`` and the indicator ``length_h`` (length of the line in box heights).

    The cases of the suite saved before that indicator existed have boxes ``size x size x 0.7 size``.
    """
    from .confidence import length_in_heights
    out = []
    for d in data:
        e = dict(d)
        e["nz"] = int(d.get("nz") or _nz(d["size"]))
        if "length_h" not in d["ind"]:
            e["ind"] = dict(d["ind"])
            e["ind"]["length_h"] = length_in_heights(d["ind"]["length"], (d["size"], d["size"], e["nz"]))
        out.append(e)
    return out

The true error of each line (err) is stored, so the "wrong line" threshold can be changed afterwards without recomputing (see relabel). checkpoint: saved after each case and resumed if interrupted.

@keeps_awake
def calibration_suite(fields=None, noises=None, sizes=(32, 48), realizations: int = 2,
                      n_seeds: int = 300, bad_threshold: float = 0.1, method: str = "lbfgs",
                      mc: int = 0, seed: int = 0, checkpoint: str | None = None,
                      verbose: bool = True, ensemble: tuple = ()) -> list:
    """Suite of calibration cases: fields × noises × resolutions × realizations.

    Each element is the result of ``solarff.confidence.calibration_case``
    plus ``field``, ``noise_model``, ``size``, ``nz``, ``realization`` and ``seconds``.
    The true error of each line (``err``) is stored, so the "wrong line"
    threshold can be changed afterwards without recomputing (see ``relabel``).
    ``checkpoint``: saved after each case and resumed if interrupted.
    """
    from .analytic import CALIBRATION_FIELDS, EXTERNAL_TEST_FIELDS, field_magnetogram
    known = {**CALIBRATION_FIELDS, **EXTERNAL_TEST_FIELDS}
    fields = list(fields or CALIBRATION_FIELDS)
    noises = list(noises or NOISE_MODELS)
    say = print if verbose else (lambda *a, **k: None)
    cases = [(f, nm, s, r) for f in fields for nm in noises for s in sizes for r in range(realizations)]
    signature = {"cases": cases, "n_seeds": n_seeds, "bad_threshold": bad_threshold,
                 "method": method, "mc": mc, "seed": seed}
    if ensemble:
        signature["ensemble"] = list(ensemble)
    state = load_checkpoint(checkpoint, signature)
    data = state["data"] if state is not None else []
    if data:
        say(f"  batería: reanudando desde {checkpoint} ({len(data)}/{len(cases)} casos hechos)")
    exact_cache = {}
    t0 = time.time()
    for i in range(len(data), len(cases)):
        fname, nm, size, r = cases[i]
        tc = time.time()
        if (fname, size) not in exact_cache:
            exact_cache = {(fname, size): known[fname](size, size, _nz(size))}
        exact = exact_cache[(fname, size)]
        sz, st = NOISE_MODELS[nm]
        k = seed * 100003 + i
        mag = field_magnetogram(exact, noise=sz, noise_t=st, rng=k)
        rec = calibration_case(exact, mag, _nz(size), n_seeds=n_seeds, bad_threshold=bad_threshold,
                               method=method, seed=k + 7, noise_bt=st, mc=mc, mc_seed=k + 13, ensemble=tuple(ensemble))
        rec.update(field=fname, noise_model=nm, size=size, realization=r, seconds=time.time() - tc)
        data.append(rec)
        say(f"  caso {i + 1}/{len(cases)}: {fname}, {nm}, {size}², real. {r}: "
            f"{rec['bad'].mean():.0%} líneas malas ({rec['seconds']:.0f}s; "
            f"total {time.time() - t0:.0f}s)", flush=True)
        if checkpoint:
            save_checkpoint(checkpoint, {"signature": signature, "data": data})
    return add_box(data)    # the cases read from a checkpoint older than ``length_h`` get it here

@keeps_awake
def proportion_suite(fields=None, boxes=PROPORTION_BOXES, noises=None, n_seeds: int = 300,
                     bad_threshold: float = 0.1, seed: int = 600011, checkpoint: str | None = None,
                     verbose: bool = True) -> list:
    """The calibration families in boxes of other proportions: fields × noises × boxes, one realization.

    All the boxes of ``calibration_suite`` are ``n x n x 0.7 n``, so a model fitted with them alone cannot tell
    a line that is long compared with the horizontal size of the box from one that is long compared with its
    height. These cases, with the same settings, break that degeneracy. Each element is the result of
    ``solarff.confidence.calibration_case`` plus ``field``, ``noise_model``, ``size``, ``nz``,
    ``realization`` (0) and ``seconds``; ``checkpoint`` as in ``calibration_suite``.
    """
    from .analytic import CALIBRATION_FIELDS, EXTERNAL_TEST_FIELDS, field_magnetogram
    known = {**CALIBRATION_FIELDS, **EXTERNAL_TEST_FIELDS}
    fields = list(fields or SIX_FAMILIES)
    noises = list(noises or NOISE_MODELS)
    # position of each family in the random seeds (that of examples/27_box_proportion.py, where these cases were first run)
    order = list(CALIBRATION_FIELDS) + ["TD-relax", "LFFF-delta"]
    order += sorted(f for f in known if f not in order)
    say = print if verbose else (lambda *a, **k: None)
    cases = [(bi, f, nm) for bi in range(len(boxes)) for f in fields for nm in noises]
    signature = {"cases": cases, "boxes": [list(b) for b in boxes], "n_seeds": n_seeds,
                 "bad_threshold": bad_threshold, "seed": seed}
    state = load_checkpoint(checkpoint, signature)
    data = state["data"] if state is not None else []
    if data:
        say(f"  proporciones: reanudando desde {checkpoint} ({len(data)}/{len(cases)} casos hechos)")
    exact_cache = {}
    t0 = time.time()
    for i in range(len(data), len(cases)):
        bi, fname, nm = cases[i]
        n, nz = boxes[bi]
        tc = time.time()
        if (fname, bi) not in exact_cache:
            exact_cache = {(fname, bi): known[fname](n, n, nz)}
        exact = exact_cache[(fname, bi)]
        sz, st = NOISE_MODELS[nm]
        k = seed + 1000 * bi + 10 * order.index(fname) + list(NOISE_MODELS).index(nm)
        mag = field_magnetogram(exact, noise=sz, noise_t=st, rng=k)
        rec = calibration_case(exact, mag, nz, n_seeds=n_seeds, bad_threshold=bad_threshold, seed=k + 7, noise_bt=st)
        rec.update(field=fname, noise_model=nm, size=n, nz=nz, realization=0, seconds=time.time() - tc)
        data.append(rec)
        say(f"  caso {i + 1}/{len(cases)}: {fname}, {nm}, {n} x {n} x {nz}: {rec['bad'].mean():.0%} líneas malas "
            f"({rec['seconds']:.0f}s; total {time.time() - t0:.0f}s)", flush=True)
        if checkpoint:
            save_checkpoint(checkpoint, {"signature": signature, "data": data})
    return data

def relabel(data: list, bad_threshold: float) -> list:
    """Copy of ``data`` with another "wrong line" threshold (relative shape error)."""
    out = []
    for d in data:

        e["bad_threshold"] = bad_threshold
        out.append(e)
    return out

def stack(data: list, features) -> tuple:
    """Design matrix, labels and groups (field, noise, size) of the valid lines."""
    X = np.vstack([_design(d["ind"], features) for d in data])
    y = np.concatenate([d["bad"] for d in data]).astype(int)
    g = {k: np.concatenate([[d.get(k)] * len(d["bad"]) for d in data])
         for k in ("field", "noise_model", "size")}
    ok = np.all(np.isfinite(X), axis=1)
    return X[ok], y[ok], {k: v[ok] for k, v in g.items()}

def ece(p, y, bins: int = 10) -> float:
    """Expected calibration error with ``bins`` equal-width bins."""
    p, y = np.asarray(p, float), np.asarray(y, float)
    idx = np.minimum((p * bins).astype(int), bins - 1)
    e = 0.0
    for b in range(bins):
        m = idx == b
        if m.any():
            e += m.mean() * abs(y[m].mean() - p[m].mean())
    return float(e)

def reliability_curve(p, y, bins: int = 10) -> dict:
    """Mean predicted probability and observed frequency per bin (reliability diagram)."""
    p, y = np.asarray(p, float), np.asarray(y, float)
    idx = np.minimum((p * bins).astype(int), bins - 1)
    pm, fo, n = [], [], []
    for b in range(bins):
        m = idx == b
        if m.sum() >= 5:
            pm.append(p[m].mean())
            fo.append(y[m].mean())
            n.append(int(m.sum()))
    return {"p": np.array(pm), "freq": np.array(fo), "n": np.array(n)}

def bootstrap_ci(p, y, metric, groups=None, n_boot: int = 500, seed: int = 0, level: float = 0.95):
    """Bootstrap confidence interval of ``metric(p, y)``.

    If ``groups`` are given (e.g. the case each line belongs to), whole
    groups are resampled: the lines of the same case are not
    independent, and resampling single lines would give intervals that are too
    narrow.
    """
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    p, y = np.asarray(p), np.asarray(y)
    vals = []
    if groups is None:
        for _ in range(n_boot):
            i = rng.integers(0, len(p), len(p))
            vals.append(metric(p[i], y[i]))
    else:
        ug = np.unique(groups)
        members = {g: np.flatnonzero(groups == g) for g in ug}
        for _ in range(n_boot):
            i = np.concatenate([members[g] for g in rng.choice(ug, len(ug))])
            vals.append(metric(p[i], y[i]))
    vals = np.asarray(vals, float)
    vals = vals[np.isfinite(vals)]
    a = (1 - level) / 2
    return float(np.quantile(vals, a)), float(np.quantile(vals, 1 - a))

def classifiers(features) -> dict:
    """Candidate classifiers: name -> (factory, needs groups in fit)."""
    from sklearn.ensemble import HistGradientBoostingClassifier, RandomForestClassifier
    from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression

                                      LogisticRegression(C=1.0, max_iter=3000)), False),
        "gb_monotone": (gb, False),
        "gb_monotone+iso": (lambda: _Isotonic(gb), True),

def cross_validate(data: list, features=USED_FEATURES, models=None, group: str = "field",
                   n_boot: int = 500, verbose: bool = True, l2: float = 1e-2) -> dict:
    """Cross-validation leaving out one value of ``group`` ("field", "noise_model" or "size").

    For each model returns the out-of-sample probabilities of all the
    lines, global AUC/Brier/ECE with bootstrap 95 % CI (resampling
    whole cases) and the metrics of each left-out group. ``l2`` is the penalty
    of the logistic regression (1e-2 in the published model; 0 = maximum likelihood).
    """
    say = print if verbose else (lambda *a, **k: None)
    features = list(features)
    X, y, G = stack(data, features)
    case_id = np.concatenate([[i] * len(d["bad"]) for i, d in enumerate(data)])
    case_id = case_id[np.all(np.isfinite(np.vstack([_design(d["ind"], features) for d in data])), axis=1)]
    groups = G[group]
    cands = classifiers(features)
    cands["logistic"] = (lambda: _Logistic(l2=l2), False)
    models = list(models or cands)
    out = {"features": features, "group": group, "y": y, "groups": groups, "case": case_id,
           "base_rate": float(y.mean()), "models": {}}
    for name in models:
        factory, needs_groups = cands[name]
        p = np.full(len(y), np.nan)
        per = {}
        for g in np.unique(groups):
            te = groups == g
            m = factory()
            if needs_groups:
                inner = G["field"][~te] if group != "field" else groups[~te]
                m.fit(X[~te], y[~te], groups=inner)
            else:
                m.fit(X[~te], y[~te])
            p[te] = m.predict_proba(X[te])[:, 1]
            per[str(g)] = {"auc": auc(p[te], y[te]), "brier": brier(p[te], y[te]),
                           "ece": ece(p[te], y[te]), "bad_rate": float(y[te].mean()), "n": int(te.sum())}
        res = {"p": p, "per_group": per}
        for mname, fn in (("auc", auc), ("brier", brier), ("ece", ece)):
            res[mname] = float(fn(p, y))
            res[mname + "_ci"] = bootstrap_ci(p, y, fn, groups=case_id, n_boot=n_boot)
        aucs = [v["auc"] for v in per.values()]
        res["auc_groups_mean"], res["auc_groups_std"] = float(np.mean(aucs)), float(np.std(aucs))
        res["reliability"] = reliability_curve(p, y)
        out["models"][name] = res
        say(f"  {name:18s} AUC {res['auc']:.3f} [{res['auc_ci'][0]:.3f}, {res['auc_ci'][1]:.3f}]  "
            f"Brier {res['brier']:.3f}  ECE {res['ece']:.3f}  "
            f"(AUC por {group}: {res['auc_groups_mean']:.3f} ± {res['auc_groups_std']:.3f})")
    return out

def single_feature_auc(data: list, features=ALL_FEATURES + ("length_h",)) -> dict:
    """AUC of each indicator separately (over all the cases)."""
    res = {}
    for k in features:
        if k not in data[0]["ind"]:
            continue
        v = np.concatenate([np.asarray(d["ind"][k], float) for d in data])
        y = np.concatenate([d["bad"] for d in data])
        res[k] = auc(FEATURE_SIGN.get(k, 1) * v, y)
    return res

def threshold_for(p_bad, y, max_bad_accepted: float = 0.2) -> float:
    """Lowest confidence threshold (1 − p) that leaves ≤ ``max_bad_accepted`` wrong lines accepted."""
    conf = 1 - np.asarray(p_bad)
    for t in np.linspace(0.05, 0.95, 91):
        acc = conf >= t
        if acc.sum() >= 10 and y[acc].mean() <= max_bad_accepted:
            return float(t)
    return 0.5

def summarize(data: list, cv: dict, single: dict | None = None) -> dict:
    """Serialisable (JSON) summary of the suite and of the cross-validations.

    ``cv``: ``{group: result of cross_validate}``. This is what the report reads.
    """
    from .utils import code_version
    bad_rate = {}
    for key in ("field", "noise_model", "size"):
        vals = sorted({d[key] for d in data}, key=str)
        bad_rate[key] = {str(v): float(np.mean(np.concatenate([d["bad"] for d in data if d[key] == v])))
                         for v in vals}
    out = {
        "n_cases": len(data), "n_lines": int(sum(len(d["bad"]) for d in data)),
        "fields": sorted({d["field"] for d in data}), "noise_models": sorted({d["noise_model"] for d in data}),
        "sizes": sorted({int(d["size"]) for d in data}),
        "realizations": int(max(d["realization"] for d in data) + 1),
        "bad_threshold": data[0]["bad_threshold"], "bad_rate": bad_rate,
        "bad_rate_field_size": {f: {str(n): float(np.mean(np.concatenate(
            [d["bad"] for d in data if d["field"] == f and d["size"] == n] or [np.array([np.nan])])))
            for n in sorted({d["size"] for d in data})} for f in sorted({d["field"] for d in data})},
        "single_auc": single or single_feature_auc(data),
        "code_version": code_version()["label"], "cv": {},
    }
    for group, res in cv.items():
        out["cv"][group] = {"features": res["features"], "base_rate": res["base_rate"], "models": {}}
        for name, r in res["models"].items():
            out["cv"][group]["models"][name] = {k: r[k] for k in (
                "auc", "auc_ci", "brier", "brier_ci", "ece", "ece_ci", "auc_groups_mean", "auc_groups_std",
                "per_group", "reliability")}
    return _jsonable(out)

The metrics, the isotonic recalibration (if isotonic) and the threshold are obtained from the predictions of the leave-one-field-out cross-validation (cv_field = cross_validate(data, group="field")), that is, always on geometries the model has not seen. threshold: minimum confidence of a "reliable" line. def fit_default(data: list, cv_field: dict, features=USED_FEATURES, isotonic: bool = False,
                threshold: float = 0.8) -> dict:
    """Default calibration fitted with the *whole* suite, and its out-of-sample metrics.

    The logistic regression is fitted with all the lines. The metrics, the
    isotonic recalibration (if ``isotonic``) and the threshold are obtained from the
    predictions of the leave-one-field-out cross-validation
    (``cv_field = cross_validate(data, group="field")``), that is, always
    on geometries the model has not seen.
    ``threshold``: minimum confidence of a "reliable" line. Since the probability
    is calibrated (ECE ≈ 0.02 out of sample), it is read literally: 0.8 =
    at most a 20 % probability that the line is wrong.
    Returns ``{"calibration": ..., "metrics": ...}`` with the same format as
    ``solarff.confidence.fit_calibration``.
    """
    features = list(features)
    X, y, _ = stack(data, features)
    cal = _fit_logistic(X, y.astype(float))
    cal.update(features=features, bad_threshold=data[0]["bad_threshold"], noise="varios")
    p_oof = np.asarray(cv_field["models"]["logistic"]["p"], float)
    if isotonic:
        from sklearn.isotonic import IsotonicRegression
        iso = IsotonicRegression(out_of_bounds="clip", y_min=0, y_max=1).fit(p_oof, y)
        grid = np.linspace(0, 1, 101)
        cal["iso_x"], cal["iso_y"] = grid.round(4).tolist(), np.round(iso.predict(grid), 4).tolist()
        p_oof = np.interp(p_oof, cal["iso_x"], cal["iso_y"])
    thr = float(threshold)
    cal["threshold"] = thr
    conf = 1 - p_oof
    acc = conf >= thr
    shape = np.concatenate([d["err"]["shape"] for d in data])
    ok = np.all(np.isfinite(np.vstack([_design(d["ind"], features) for d in data])), axis=1)
    shape = shape[ok]
    metrics = {
        "auc_combined": auc(p_oof, y), "auc_features": single_feature_auc(data),
        "threshold": thr, "bad_fraction_all": float(y.mean()),
        "bad_fraction_accepted": float(y[acc].mean()) if acc.any() else float("nan"),
        "accepted_fraction": float(acc.mean()),
        "error_median_accepted": float(np.nanmedian(shape[acc])) if acc.any() else float("nan"),
        "error_median_rejected": float(np.nanmedian(shape[~acc])) if (~acc).any() else float("nan"),
        "brier": brier(p_oof, y), "ece": ece(p_oof, y),
    }
    groups = np.asarray(cv_field["groups"])
    per = {}
    for g in np.unique(groups):
        m = groups == g
        per[str(g)] = {"accepted": float(acc[m].mean()),
                       "bad_accepted": float(y[m][acc[m]].mean()) if acc[m].any() else float("nan"),
                       "bad_all": float(y[m].mean())}
    metrics["per_field"] = per
    metrics["bad_accepted_worst_field"] = float(np.nanmax([v["bad_accepted"] for v in per.values()]))
    return {"calibration": cal, "metrics": metrics}
